2026-04-29.text:
Bright sun and a red Specialized bike on the planks of Avila Beach Pier set the tone for a coastal ride that stretched south through Pismo Beach by afternoon.

**Highlights:**

- [Avila Beach Pier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avila_Beach,_California) — one of the few California piers inside a sheltered cove, giving it unusually calm, turquoise water compared to open-coast piers
- [Pismo Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pismo_Beach,_California) — its sea arches are carved from Pismo Formation mudstone, a marine sedimentary layer roughly 15–20 million years old
- [Dinosaur Caves Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_Caves_Park) — named for a life-sized concrete dinosaur that once stood here as a roadside attraction; the blufftop park now overlooks tide pools and a lone pine-crowned sandstone stack

2026-04-30.text:
Rust and salt air defined the morning, with a graffiti-tagged wreck listing in the shallows below the coastal bluffs before we drove south to the famously tiny hamlet of Harmony for lunch and a detour into roadside Americana.

**Highlights:**

- [SS Montebello (shipwreck)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Montebello) — a tanker torpedoed by a Japanese submarine in 1941, its corroded hull still visible near Cayucos with graffiti covering the wheelhouse
- [Cayucos Pier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cayucos,_California) — one of California's oldest recreational piers, visible stretching into the bay behind the wreck
- [Harmony, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmony,_California) — an unincorporated community with a self-reported population of 18, once home to a dairy cooperative and now operating as a boutique arts village

2026-05-01.text:
Ornate tile fountains and cascading bougainvillea greeted us at the hilltop estate before we descended to the coast for seals and pelicans in the early afternoon.

**Highlights:**
- [Hearst Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hearst_Castle) — William Randolph Hearst assembled the Neptune Pool using fragments of a genuine ancient Roman temple imported from Europe; the estate's 165 rooms took nearly 28 years to complete.
- [Neptune Pool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neptune_Pool) — drained and rebuilt three times by Hearst himself, it holds 345,000 gallons and is lined with Vermont marble.
- [Piedras Blancas elephant seal rookery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piedras_Blancas_elephant_seal_rookery) — established only in 1990, it now hosts over 17,000 seals annually, making it one of the most accessible rookeries in the world.

2026-05-02.text:
Overcast afternoon light made the folk-art stumps at Moonstone Beach oddly vivid before we drove inland to watch Sensorio's fiber-optic fields ignite at dusk.

**Highlights:**

- [Moonstone Beach Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonstone_Beach) — a narrow coastal strip in Cambria known for its wave-polished moonstones washing ashore; local artists have tucked whimsical carved stump faces into the trailside vegetation
- [Sensorio Field of Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensorio) — Bruce Munro's Paso Robles installation uses roughly 58,800 solar-powered fiber-optic stems across 15 acres of rolling oak savanna; Munro first developed the Field of Light concept during a 1992 visit to Uluru, Australia

2026-05-03.text:
Misty light hung over the coast as we pulled off CA-1 to catch the McWay Falls overlook after brunch at Hidden Kitchen in Big Sur.

**Highlights:**

- [McWay Falls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McWay_Falls) — one of the only tidefalls in California, the 80-foot drop lands directly onto a beach that is completely inaccessible to visitors, keeping the sand permanently undisturbed
- [Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_Pfeiffer_Burns_State_Park) — named after a pioneer rancher who spent her entire life in Big Sur; the overlook trail requires only a short walk yet delivers one of the coast's most photographed views
